facts.text: Lisbon was named by John Moore after Lisbon, Portugal, a tribute that still echoes in the village’s name.
The village joined Kendall County in 1841, marking its official entry into Illinois statehood.
A post office, schoolhouse, and early enterprise appeared together, signaling Lisbon’s first steps toward a self‑sufficient community.
Today Lisbon hosts the Lisbon Consolidated School, a modern hub for local education that traces its roots back to the village’s original schoolhouse.
John Moore Park offers a green escape for residents, while the nearby West Lisbon Church and Lisbon Bethlehem Lutheran Church reflect the village’s long‑standing religious heritage.
Lisbon’s geographic coordinates place it at 41°28′50″N 88°28′58″W, a spot that has guided travelers for generations.
